l3_edits.old: How many minimum subscriptions do you need to buy in order to have the opportunity to watch episodes of purchased shows d (1 ≤ d ≤ n) days in a row? In other words, you want to buy the minimum number of TV shows so that there is some segment of d consecutive days in which all episodes belong to the purchased shows.
l3_edits.new: For each segment of d (1 ≤ d ≤ n) consecutive days, count the minimum number of show subscriptions needed to watch every episode in that segment. Find the maximum of this count over all such segments.

l3_edits.old: The answer to a test case is the minimum number of TV shows for which you need to purchase a subscription so that you can watch episodes of the purchased TV shows on BerTV for d consecutive days. Please note that it is permissible that you will be able to watch more than d days in a row.
l3_edits.new: The answer to a test case is the maximum number of distinct TV shows among all segments of exactly d consecutive days.

sample_explanation_policy: Original sample inputs retained in full. Outputs regenerated using isolated L3 reference. Old output-dependent explanations replaced; post-sample definitions and constraints retained.
